Śaṅkhatīrtha, a tīrtha on the Sarasvatī. § 615f (Baladevat.): Here Baladeva beheld a gigantic tree, Mahāśaṅkha, tall as Meru, looking like Śvetaparvata, and resorted to by many Ṛ.; there dwell Y., Vd., Rā., Pś., and Si., in thousands; all of them, abandoning other kinds of food, observe vows and regulations, and take at due seasons the fruits of that tree for their sustenance, and wander unseen by men: IX, 37, 2137.
